body: You're right about the comma after spread, but the comma dangle error persists even after removing it.
Thanks for the fast response and fix 👍🏻

@sstur That part is actually intended; your code's syntax is invalid, so it wouldn't make sense for ESLint to require a trailing comma in that case. The error reported there is a result of the bugfix in https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/7297.

Oh, I see. I believe my syntax is valid for Stage 3 of ECMAScript and is handled for us by Babel. We use ESLint with some newer ECMAScript proposed features such as this (specifically we use the same ES feature set as ReactNative.) It has been working as long as I can remember but broke when upgrading from 3.7.1 to 3.8.0 (presumably because of the bugfix you referenced).

I am sticking to 3.7.1 now but probably need a way forward with proposed, not-yet-standardized features.

I understand that you're using babel, but a trailing comma after a rest property is not valid syntax even according to the [current proposal spec](https://sebmarkbage.github.io/ecmascript-rest-spread/), because there is nothing that could follow a rest property.

The same thing applies with the already-standardized rest elements:

``` js
const [
  foo,
  ...bar, // <-- This is a syntax error in ES6
] = baz;
```

In order to be more compliant with the spec, babel's parser [temporarily reported this as a syntax error](https://github.com/babel/babylon/releases/tag/v6.11.3), but it was [later reverted](https://github.com/babel/babylon/releases/tag/v6.11.4) due to breakage.

The fix in this case is to simply remove the comma, so that it becomes valid syntax according to the Stage 3 proposal.

Oh, I see! This I did not know!

So Babel is being more liberal than the standards in what it accepts. Interesting.

Thank you for taking the time to explain this. I wonder how to get the word out there so people don't continue opening issues..

issue.body:
After updating from `eslint@3.7.0` to `eslint@3.8.0`, I am now suddenly getting errors whenever I have `...rest,` when destructuring an object, e.g.:

``` javascript
const {
  prop1,
  ...rest, // Unexpected trailing comma  comma-dangle
} = obj
```

```
 error  Unexpected trailing comma  comma-dangle
```

If I revert back to `eslint@3.7.0` the error disappears.

Here's the [eslintrc I'm using](https://github.com/blockai/eslint-config-blockai):

``` javascript
module.exports = {
  extends: 'airbnb-base',
  parser: 'babel-eslint',
  rules: {
    'consistent-return': 0,
    'no-param-reassign': [2, { props: false }],
    semi: [2, 'never'],
    camelcase: 0,
    'no-underscore-dangle': 0,
  },
}
```

issue.title: Add opt-in usage tracking for blocks added to post content

repository.name: gutenberg
repository.description: The Block Editor project for WordPress and beyond. Plugin is available from the official repository.

issue.body:
This PR asks users for permission to enable usage tracking:

![2017-08-01t18 15 11-0400](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/227022/28849519-5eca0154-76e5-11e7-8991-66ee95a58418.png)

When the user clicks "Yes" or "No", the preference is stored using the existing WordPress method of saving user preferences (the `setUserSetting` function [used elsewhere in wp-admin](https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/search?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=setUserSetting&type=); props @swissspidy for telling us about this function in #1948).  This preference is saved as a cookie and eventually [persisted as a user option](https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/blob/4.8.0/src/wp-includes/option.php#L817-L833).

If the user clicks "Yes", tracking events will be recorded using existing WP.com infrastructure every time a block is added to the editor.  The approach taken here is very similar to [Calypso's event tracking code](https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/blob/a261ec0/client/lib/analytics/index.js#L140).

We can use the data added in this PR to inform various decisions such as default order for blocks and whether some blocks are less suitable for core, and more generally this is a very useful technique to collect user experience data.
